title: Near or far: where do 1/d links land?
hook: If nearer links are likelier, most links should be short. Are they?

doesNotKnow: why: with chance ∝ 1/d, a link is equally likely to land 1–2, 2–4, … or 256–512 away

misconception: With 1/d links most links are very short.
objective: The learner can explain that with chance ∝ 1/d each doubling band of distances holds twice as many distances, each half as likely, so every band gets about the same share of links (2–3 away: 12.2%; 256–512 away: 10.2% on a ring of 1,024).

claims.text: With chance ∝ 1/d on a ring of 1,024, the band 2–3 away gets 12.2% of links and the band 256–512 away gets 10.2%.
claims.source: Demo.tsx shares(): exact sums over d = 1..512 with 2 people at each d < 512 and 1 at d = 512, weight (people at d)/d, bands 1, 2–3, 4–7, …, 128–255, 256–512. Builder's Node run 2026-10-14: 14.7, 12.2, 11.1, 10.6, 10.4, 10.3, 10.2, 10.2, 10.2 (%). Matches the brief's check.

claims.text: With 1/d links, every band from 2–3 out gets 10–12% of links.
claims.source: Same sums as c1: bands 2 to 9 range from 12.2% down to 10.2%; the band of distance 1 alone gets 14.7%.

claims.text: Each band holds twice as many distances as the one before, and with 1/d each of those distances is half as likely, so the two cancel.
claims.source: Band [2^k, 2^(k+1)) has 2^k distances, each with weight between 2^-(k+1) and 2^-k, so its total weight is between 1/2 and 1 for every k (it tends to ln 2 ≈ 0.69 of a unit).

claims.text: Uniform links put 50.1% of links in the farthest band (256–512); 1/d² links put 60.9% at distance 1.
claims.source: Demo.tsx shares() with q = 0 and q = 2: uniform 513 of 1,023 people are 256–512 away = 50.1%; 1/d² band 1 = 2/(sum of people(d)/d²) = 60.9% (builder's Node run, 2026-10-14).

claims.text: Wherever a message is, a link that halves its remaining distance is about equally likely; that is why 1/d links route fast.
claims.source: Easley and Kleinberg (2010) ch. 20 (advanced material on decentralised search); Kleinberg (2000), Nature 406 and STOC 2000. From the brief; builder has not opened these. Attribution: fact-checker confirms.

recall.question: Long links land at distance d with chance ∝ 1/d. Which is more likely: a link 4–7 away, or one 128–255 away?
recall.why: The far band holds 32 times as many distances, but each is about 32 times less likely, so the two bands get about the same share (11.1% vs 10.2% on a ring of 1,024).
